mainTopic: When a borrower becomes responsible for a borrowed item: a cow sent with the lender's slave, and when a borrowed ax is locked in
overview: The משנה ruled that if the borrower agreed to have the cow sent with the lender's slave and it died on the way, the borrower is liable. The גמרא asks: isn't a slave's hand like his master's hand? שמואל answers that the משנה means an עבד עברי. רב says that even an עבד כנעני fits, because it is like telling the lender 'hit it with a stick and it will come.' A ברייתא rules that sending the cow with a slave leaves the borrower exempt, which challenges רב. רב answers that the משנה is a case where the borrower actually said those words, and the גמרא quotes רב's ruling on that case. A ברייתא that seems to support רב is pushed aside by רב אשי as a special case of courtyards. The גמרא then turns to רב הונא, who says a borrowed ax is locked in only once the borrower chops with it. It shows that רבי אמי and רבי אלעזר, together with a ברייתא, disagree with him, and that ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why is the borrower liable if the slave's hand is like the master's?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's ruling that the borrower is liable when the cow is sent with the lender's slave, since a slave's hand counts as his master's hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The משנה said that if it was sent with his slave, the borrower is liable. But a slave's hand is like his master's hand!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes one case from the משנה and attacks it. If the lender's slave is holding the cow, it seems the lender is still holding it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that whatever a slave holds counts as held by his master. So while the slave is walking the cow, it should still be in the lender's possession, and if it dies the lender should lose, not the borrower. Yet the משנה says the borrower is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
His slave (here: the lender's slave)
Liable, must pay
A slave's hand is like his master's hand: what he holds, his master holds

phrases.english: Gemara: 'By the hand of his slave, he is liable,'
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: the borrower agreed to have the cow sent with the lender's slave, and it died on the way.

phrases.english: But the hand of a slave is like the hand of his master!

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּיַד עַבְדּוֹ – חַיָּיב, יַד עֶבֶד כְּיַד רַבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by questioning a case in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the borrower is liable when the cow is sent with the lender's slave.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since יד עבד כיד רבו, the cow in the slave's hand is still in the lender's possession, so the borrower should not yet carry the risk.

steps.title: שמואל: the משנה means a Hebrew slave
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that the משנה is speaking of an עבד עברי, whose body is not owned by his master, so his hand is not his master's hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: The משנה means a Hebrew slave, whose body the master does not own.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question by narrowing which slave the משנה means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'a slave's hand is like his master's hand' only works when the master owns the slave's body. An עבד עברי is only hired out for his work, not owned, so the cow in his hand has really left the lender, and the borrower is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: A Jewish slave who serves for a limited time
Acquires his body: owns the person himself

phrases.english: Shmuel said: It is speaking of a Hebrew slave,
whose body the master does not acquire.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) to a specific type of slave.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The slave in the משנה is any slave, so his hand should count as the lender's hand.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means an עבד עברי, whose body the master doesn't own, so the rule of יד עבד כיד רבו does not apply.

steps.title: רב: even a Canaanite slave, like 'hit it with a stick'
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that even with an עבד כנעני the borrower is liable, because sending it with the slave is like telling the lender to hit the cow with a stick so it walks over by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: You can even say the משנה means a Canaanite slave. It is as if the borrower told him: 'Hit it with a stick and it will come.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a different answer that keeps the משנה about a regular, owned slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב agrees an עבד כנעני's hand is his master's hand, but says that does not matter here. Since the borrower asked for it to be sent this way, the slave is just like a stick pushing the cow toward the borrower. Once the cow leaves the lender's domain on the borrower's request, the borrower carries the risk.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say: introduces a broader answer
A non-Jewish slave fully owned by his master
Hit it with a stick

steps.confusionAlert: רב is not saying a Canaanite slave's hand stops being his master's hand. He is saying that in this case the slave is treated like a tool that just moves the cow along.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא בְּעֶבֶד כְּנַעֲנִי,
phrases.english: Rav said: You can even say it is speaking of a Canaanite slave,
it is considered as if the borrower said to him:
'Hit it with a stick, and it will come.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא בְּעֶבֶד כְּנַעֲנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 1, different from שמואל's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the case through an analogy.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With an owned slave, the cow stays in the lender's possession.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the borrower asked for this, the slave is like a stick driving the cow; once it leaves the lender's domain, the borrower is liable.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the borrower is exempt with the slave
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: if the cow is sent with the lender's son or agent the borrower is liable, but if with his slave the borrower is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: If someone borrows a cow and the lender sent it with his son or his agent, the borrower is liable. With his slave, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to say the opposite of the משנה about the slave. This sets up the next step, which shows whom it challenges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא agrees about the son and the agent. But about the slave it says exempt, which fits the rule that a slave's hand is his master's hand. That clashes with the משנה's 'liable.'

keyTerms.meaning: The borrower
His agent, messenger
Exempt, does not pay

phrases.english: They raised an objection: One who borrows the cow

phrases.aramaic: וְשִׁלְּחָהּ לוֹ בְּיַד בְּנוֹ, בְּיַד שְׁלוּחוֹ – חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: and the lender sent it to him by his son, or by his agent: the borrower is liable.
By his slave: he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an outside source that clashes with the משנה as explained by the two answers.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the borrower is liable when the cow is sent by the slave.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says exempt for the slave, directly opposite the משנה.

steps.title: שמואל can explain it, but רב is left with a difficulty
steps.stepSummary: For שמואל, the משנה is an עבד עברי and the ברייתא an עבד כנעני. For רב, who said the משנה means an עבד כנעני, the ברייתא is a difficulty.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for שמואל: the משנה is about a Hebrew slave, and the ברייתא is about a Canaanite slave. But for רב, it is a difficulty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows which answer the ברייתא hurts: שמואל is fine, but רב is challenged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל can split the sources: an עבד עברי's hand is not his master's (liable), while an עבד כנעני's hand is (exempt). רב said even an עבד כנעני makes the borrower liable, so the ברייתא's 'exempt' contradicts him.

keyTerms.meaning: It is fine for: this view has no problem
A teaching of the תנאים not included in the משנה
But: introduces the side with the problem
It is a difficulty

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל: משנה = עבד עברי (liable), ברייתא = עבד כנעני (exempt). רב said the משנה could be an עבד כנעני, so the ברייתא challenges him.

phrases.english: It is fine according to Shmuel:
our Mishnah is about a Hebrew slave,
the baraita is about a Canaanite slave.
But according to Rav, it is a difficulty!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the force of the ברייתא from step 4 against the two answers.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's answer that the משנה can be about an עבד כנעני.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא rules exempt with a slave; if it is an עבד כנעני, it contradicts רב's claim that the borrower is liable even then.

steps.title: רב's revised answer: the borrower really said 'hit it with a stick'
steps.stepSummary: רב changes his answer. The משנה is not 'like' a case where the borrower said 'hit it with a stick.' It is a case where he actually said it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב can tell you: don't say it is as if he said 'hit it with a stick.' Say instead that he really did say to him: 'Hit it with a stick and it will come.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the ברייתא's challenge to רב by changing the wording of רב's answer. In the משנה, the borrower actually told the lender to just hit the cow and send it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, רב said that sending the cow with an עבד כנעני is 'like' telling the lender to hit it with a stick, and that clashed with the ברייתא. Now רב limits the משנה to a case where the borrower said those words out loud. When he didn't say them, as in the ברייתא, the slave's hand is still the lender's hand, and the borrower is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't say... rather say: a formula for changing the wording of an earlier statement
It is considered as if he said to him
In a case where he actually said to him
Hit it with a stick: send the cow off on its own

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the tiny difference between כְּאָמַר ('as if he said') and בְּאָמַר ('where he said'). One letter changes רב's whole answer.

phrases.english: Rav can say to you:
Do not say 'it is considered as if he said to him,'
phrases.notes: This is the wording of רב's answer back in step 3.

phrases.english: rather say: 'where he actually said to him,'
'Hit it with a stick and it will come.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב: לָא תֵּימָא נַעֲשָׂה כְּאָמַר לוֹ, אֶלָּא אֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty raised against רב in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the wording of the earlier answer so that the משנה covers a narrower case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Sending the cow with any slave is automatically like 'hit it with a stick,' which clashes with the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is a case where the borrower actually said 'hit it with a stick.' The ברייתא is a case where he did not.

steps.title: רב's ruling on the 'hit it with a stick' case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רב's ruling: when the borrower says 'hit it with a stick and it will come,' he is liable as soon as the cow leaves the lender's domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was stated: 'Lend me your cow.' He answered, 'With whom should I send it?' He said, 'Hit it with a stick and it will come.' רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה in the name of רב: once it left the lender's domain and died, the borrower is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the new version of רב's answer. It shows that רב has a ruling on exactly this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Telling the lender to just send the cow off means the borrower takes responsibility for the trip. So the borrower is liable from the moment the cow leaves the lender's property, even before it reaches him. This explains why the borrower in the משנה is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Lend me
By whose hand: with whom should I send it?
The lender's domain or property

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that a borrower who says 'just send it' takes on liability from the moment the animal leaves the lender's property.

phrases.english: As it was stated:
'Lend me your cow,'
and he said to him: 'By whose hand?'
and he said to him: 'Hit it with a stick and it will come.'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said that Rabba bar Avuh said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁיָּצָאת מֵרְשׁוּת מַשְׁאִיל וּמֵתָה – חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: Once it left the domain of the lender and died, he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the ruling that step 6's answer depends on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the borrower said 'hit it with a stick and it will come,' he is liable once the cow leaves the lender's domain.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to support רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that a ברייתא with the same case and the same ruling supports רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this supports him? 'Lend me your cow.' He answered, 'With whom?' He said, 'Hit it with a stick and it will come.' Once it left the lender's domain and died, the borrower is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as רב, and asks whether it proves his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא has the identical case and ruling. If it holds up, רב's ruling has the support of a תנאי source. The word נימא hints that the proof may not stand.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say this supports him? A suggested proof that may be rejected
It died
Liable: must pay

phrases.english: Shall we say this supports him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' means רב, from the ruling just quoted.

phrases.english: 'Lend me your cow,'
and he said to him: 'By whose hand?'

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר לוֹ: הַכִּישָׁהּ בְּמַקֵּל וְהִיא תָּבֹא.
phrases.english: and he said to him: 'Hit it with a stick and it will come.'

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁיָּצָאת מֵרְשׁוּת מַשְׁאִיל וּמֵתָה – חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: Once it left the domain of the lender and died, he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers outside support for רב's ruling in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that the borrower is liable once the cow leaves the lender's domain.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the identical case and ruling.

steps.title: רב אשי: the ברייתא is a special case
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rejects the proof. The ברייתא may be a case where the borrower's courtyard lies further in than the lender's, so the cow will surely walk straight to the borrower.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: here we are dealing with a case where the borrower's courtyard was further in than the lender's courtyard. So when the lender sends the cow, it will certainly go there.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי says the ברייתא does not prove רב's ruling. It could be talking about a special layout of the courtyards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the cow leaves the lender's yard and the only way forward leads to the borrower's yard, it is certain to get there. That is why the borrower is willing to take responsibility right away. In an ordinary case the cow could wander, so the ברייתא tells us nothing about רב's broader ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? A formula that limits a source to a specific case
The borrower's courtyard
Further inside than
It will certainly go there

steps.whatToRemember: רב's ruling stands on its own. The ברייתא may be a special case where the cow's path leads only to the borrower, so it cannot prove רב's ruling.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
With what are we dealing here?
For example, where the courtyard of the borrower was
further in than the courtyard of the lender,
phrases.notes: Picture the cow leaving the lender's yard with nowhere to go except into the borrower's yard.

phrases.english: so that when he sends it,
it certainly goes there.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the support offered in step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. רב's ruling itself is not challenged.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא could be a special case where the cow is sure to reach the borrower, so it cannot prove the general rule.

steps.title: If the cow will surely come, why teach it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אשי's reading. If the cow will surely walk straight to the borrower, the ruling is obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is the point of saying it?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב אשי's explanation from Step 9. If the cow will definitely walk right to the borrower, why does the ברייתא bother to state this?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי said the borrower's courtyard lies further in, so the cow surely reaches him. But then of course the borrower is liable, and there is nothing new to learn. A ברייתא is not supposed to teach something obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, if that is really the case
What is the point of saying it? It's obvious

phrases.english: If so, what is the point of saying it?!
phrases.notes: 'If so' points to רב אשי's case, where the borrower's courtyard is further in, so the cow surely walks to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading of the ברייתא offered in the דחיה of Step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's reading of the ברייתא (the borrower's courtyard lies further in)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the cow will surely arrive, the borrower's liability is obvious, so the ברייתא would be teaching nothing new

steps.title: A path with corners where the cow might stop
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is needed for a path with corners. There, one might think the borrower does not trust the cow to arrive. The ברייתא teaches that he does trust it.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where there are corners. You might have said: he does not rely on it, because perhaps the cow will stand there and not come straight. So it teaches us that he does rely on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The ברייתא is talking about a path with corners, where the cow could wander off and stop.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With corners on the way, you might think the borrower does not count on the cow reaching him, so he does not take responsibility yet. The ברייתא teaches that he still relies on the cow coming, so he takes on liability as soon as it leaves the lender's property. That is the new lesson, so the ברייתא is not obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for a specific case
Corners, nooks along the way
You might have said (a mistaken first thought)
He relies on it, he trusts it will happen
It teaches us

steps.whatToRemember: Even when the cow could stop in a corner, the borrower trusts it will reach him. So according to this reading of the ברייתא, he is liable as soon as it leaves the lender's domain.

phrases.english: No, it is needed where there are corners.
You might have said: he does not rely on it,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the borrower. The question is whether he counts on the cow reaching him.

phrases.english: because perhaps it will stand there
and not come, walking straight;
so it teaches us that he does rely on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 10 and saves רב אשי's rejection of the proof
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With corners on the way, the borrower does not count on the cow arriving, so he would not yet be liable
steps.terutzMaskana: Even with corners, the borrower relies on the cow arriving, so he is liable

steps.title: A borrowed ax is acquired once it is used
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that a borrower of an ax acquires it only once he chops with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: one who borrows an ax from his friend: if he chopped with it, he acquired it. If he did not chop with it, he did not acquire it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. רב הונא gives a rule about when a borrower 'acquires' a borrowed ax.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב הונא, the borrowing takes hold only through using the ax, by chopping. Simply receiving it is not enough. The rule does not yet say what 'acquired' means, and the next step asks exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: Ax
Chopped, split (wood)
He acquired it

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
One who borrows an ax from his friend,
if he chopped with it, he acquired it;
if he did not chop with it, he did not acquire it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: הַשּׁוֹאֵל קַרְדּוֹם מֵחֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic, still about when a borrowing takes effect
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A borrowed ax is acquired by the borrower only once he chops with it

steps.title: Acquired for what? Not for accidents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'acquired' means. It rejects the idea that it refers to liability for accidents, because a borrowed cow is the borrower's responsibility right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what? If you say for accidents, what is different about a cow, where he is liable from the moment of borrowing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רב הונא meant by 'acquired.' It tests one answer, accidents, and shows that answer does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'acquired' meant becoming responsible for accidents, then a borrower of an ax would be liable only after chopping. But a borrower of a cow is liable from the moment he borrows it, even before using it. There is no reason an ax should be different, so this reading is rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: For what purpose? In what way?
If you say
Accidents the borrower could not prevent
What is different?
From the moment of borrowing

phrases.english: For what?
If you say it is for accidents,
what is different about a cow, where it is from the moment of borrowing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the meaning of 'קנאו' in רב הונא's rule
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of 'acquiring' רב הונא means: liability for accidents, or something else

steps.title: It means the lender can no longer back out
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא means that once the borrower chops, the lender cannot take back his agreement to lend. Before that, he can.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is about backing out. If he chopped with it, the lender cannot back out. If he did not chop with it, the lender can back out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct meaning of רב הונא's rule. 'Acquired' is about whether the lender may still change his mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the borrower has started using the ax, the loan is locked in for him, and the lender cannot take it back. Before any chopping, the loan is not yet firm, so the lender may still back out.

keyTerms.meaning: Backing out, retracting
The lender
He can back out of it

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא: chopping with the ax locks in the loan, so the lender can no longer back out. It is not about liability for accidents.

phrases.english: Rather, it is about backing out:

phrases.aramaic: בִּקַּע בּוֹ – לָא מָצֵי הָדַר בֵּיהּ מַשְׁאִיל,
phrases.english: if he chopped with it, the lender cannot back out;

phrases.aramaic: לֹא בִּקַּע בּוֹ – מָצֵי מַשְׁאִיל הָדַר בֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: if he did not chop with it, the lender can back out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the accepted meaning after the rejected reading in Step 13
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Acquired' refers to the lender losing the right to back out once the borrower has chopped

steps.title: רב הונא disagrees with רבי אמי about a הקדש ax
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רב הונא's view argues with רבי אמי. רבי אמי says that lending out a הקדש ax is already מעילה, and the borrower may chop with it from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this disagrees with רבי אמי, for רבי אמי said: one who lends out an ax of הקדש has committed מעילה, according to the benefit he gets from it. And his friend is permitted to chop with it from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רב הונא's rule clashes with a ruling of רבי אמי, and quotes that ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי holds that the lender commits מעילה at the moment he lends the ax, before any chopping. That suggests the loan takes full effect right when the ax is handed over. רב הונא, though, holds that until the borrower chops, the loan is not firm and the lender can still back out.

keyTerms.meaning: And it disagrees
Property belonging to the בית המקדש
He committed מעילה, misuse of הקדש
The small benefit of being the one who chooses whom to give to
From the start, permitted even beforehand

steps.confusionAlert: The one who commits מעילה here is the lender, not the borrower. That is why the borrower may go ahead and chop.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows two views of when a loan takes effect: right at handing over (רבי אמי), or only once the item is used (רב הונא).

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rabbi Ami,
phrases.notes: 'This' is רב הונא's rule from the last step.

phrases.english: for Rabbi Ami said:
One who lends out an ax of consecrated property
has committed misuse, according to the benefit he has from it,
and his friend is permitted to chop with it from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפְלִיגָא דְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets רב הונא's explained rule against an opposing view
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lending a הקדש ax is מעילה by the lender at the moment of lending, and the borrower may chop with it from the start

steps.title: Why רבי אמי must hold that the borrower acquires right away
steps.stepSummary: If the borrower had not acquired the ax yet, there would be no מעילה, and he could not chop with it from the start. So רבי אמי holds that the lending is complete as soon as the borrower takes the ax.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the borrower did not acquire the ax yet, why did the lender commit מעילה? And why may the borrower chop with it from the start? He could just give it back without acquiring it, and then there would be no מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves its claim from Step 15 that רבי אמי disagrees with רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעילה happens only once the borrower really takes hold of the הקדש ax, so that it leaves the Temple's possession. If the loan took hold only through chopping, the lender would not yet have committed מעילה, and the borrower's chopping would be the very act that causes it, so he should give the ax back instead (נַיהְדְּרֵיהּ). Since רבי אמי says there is already מעילה and the borrower may chop right away, the borrowing must be final the moment he takes the ax, unlike רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: He acquired it (here: the borrower took full hold of the borrowed item)
He committed מעילה, misusing הקדש property
From the start; right away
Let him give it back

phrases.english: And if he did not acquire it,
phrases.notes: "He" here is the borrower, who took the הקדש ax but has not chopped with it yet.

phrases.english: why has he committed מעילה?
phrases.notes: Now "he" means the lender, the one who lent out the הקדש ax.

to chop with it from the outset?
Let him return it and not acquire it,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It explains and proves the claim in Step 15 that רבי אמי's ruling conflicts with רב הונא.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אמי holds the borrower acquires the item immediately, which goes against רב הונא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אמי's own ruling that lending a הקדש ax is already מעילה and that the borrower may chop right away.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: a שומר's role also starts with pulling
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא's view also argues with רבי אלעזר. רבי אלעזר says that pulling (משיכה) works for שומרים just as it works for buyers.
steps.simpleTranslation: This argues with רבי אלעזר. רבי אלעזר said: just as the Sages made pulling the way buyers acquire, they also made pulling the way שומרים take on their role.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second opinion that disagrees with רב הונא: the view of רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A buyer's purchase becomes final once he pulls the item. רבי אלעזר says a שומר (a borrower is one kind of שומר) is the same: once he pulls the item, the arrangement is final. That means the lender cannot back out after the pulling, even before the borrower uses the item, which goes against רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: It argues with; it disagrees with
Pulling an item toward oneself, a way of making a deal final
Buyers
People who guard or hold someone else's item (including borrowers)

phrases.english: And it disagrees with Rabbi Elazar,
phrases.notes: "It" is רב הונא's ruling about the ax from Step 12.

phrases.english: as Rabbi Elazar said:
In the same way that they instituted pulling for buyers,
so they instituted pulling for bailees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After showing that רבי אמי disagrees with רב הונא, the גמרא names a second אמורא who also disagrees.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שומר's arrangement becomes final through משיכה, just like a purchase.

steps.title: A ברייתא teaches רבי אלעזר's idea
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the same thing as רבי אלעזר: pulling works for שומרים just as it does for buyers. It then begins a further comparison.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught in a ברייתא: just as the Sages made pulling the way buyers acquire, they also made pulling the way שומרים take on their role. And just as...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports רבי אלעזר by quoting a ברייתא that says the same thing. The ברייתא's next comparison begins here and continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now רבי אלעזר's view is not just one אמורא's opinion. It matches a ברייתא, which carries more weight. That makes the challenge to רב הונא stronger. The last word, "and just as," opens a new comparison that continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (in a ברייתא), supporting the previous statement
They (the Sages) instituted; they set up as a rule

phrases.english: This is also taught in a ברייתא:

and just as
